pr_title: rehash.c: Do not use NAME_MAX limit
pr_body:
On some systems it is too small although the system allows longer filenames.

Fixes #22886
pr_comments: Any reason not to use `_XOPEN_NAME_MAX` instead of getting the longest filename in the dir?

> Any reason not to use `_XOPEN_NAME_MAX` instead of getting the longest filename in the dir?

I do not think there is any point in hardcoding any limit when it is not necessary to do so.

> > Any reason not to use `_XOPEN_NAME_MAX` instead of getting the longest filename in the dir?
> 
> I do not think there is any point in hardcoding any limit when it is not necessary to do so.

I see, since it is dynamic, it should not exceed what the OS thinks is right.
This pull request is ready to merge
Merged to the master, 3.2, 3.1, and 3.0 branches. Thank you for the reviews.

issue_context.title: openssl-rehash(1) suffers from too short NAME_MAX on HP-UX
issue_context.body:
Note: This applies to all branches, from master to 1.1.1

Consider the following example:
```
osipovmi@deblndw024v:~
$ uname -a
HP-UX deblndw0 B.11.31 U ia64 HP-UX
osipovmi@deblndw024v:~
$ cat limits.c
# include <unistd.h>
# include <stdio.h>
# include <limits.h>
# include <errno.h>
# include <string.h>
# include <ctype.h>
# include <sys/stat.h>

int main(void) {
        #ifdef _XOPEN_PATH_MAX
        printf("_XOPEN_PATH_MAX: %d\n", _XOPEN_PATH_MAX);
        #endif
        #ifdef PATH_MAX
        printf("PATH_MAX: %d\n", PATH_MAX);
        #endif
        #ifdef _XOPEN_NAME_MAX
        printf("_XOPEN_NAME_MAX: %d\n", _XOPEN_NAME_MAX);
        #endif
        #ifdef NAME_MAX
        printf("NAME_MAX: %d\n", NAME_MAX);
        #endif
}
osipovmi@deblndw024v:~
$ cc -o limits limits.c -v
 /opt/aCC/lbin/ecom -architecture 32 -ia64abi all -ext on -lang c,c99 -exception off -sysdir /usr/include -ansi_for_scope on -inline_power 1 -link_type dynamic -fpeval float -fpevaldec _Decimal32 -tls_dyn on -target_os 11.31 --sys_include /usr/include -D_BIND_LIBCALLS -D_Math_errhandling=MATH_ERREXCEPT -D__hpux -D__unix -D__ia64=1 -D__ia64__=1 -D_BIG_ENDIAN=1 -D_ILP32 -D__STDC_VERSION__=199901L -D__STDC_HOSTED__ -D__STDC_IEC_559__ -D__STDC_IEC_559_COMPLEX__ -D__HP_cc=62900 -D__STDC_EXT__ -D_HPUX_SOURCE -D_INCLUDE_LONGLONG -D_INLINE_ASM -D_FLT_EVAL_METHOD=0 -D_DEC_EVAL_METHOD=0 -ucode hdriver=optlevel%1% -plusolistoption -Ol06all! -plusolistoption -Ol12direct! -plusolistoption -Ol13moderate! -plusooption -Oq01,al,ag,cn,sz,ic,vo,Mf,Po,es,rs,Rf,Pr,sp,in,cl,om,vc,pi,fa,pe,rr,pa,pv,nf,cp,lx,Pg,ug,lu,lb,uj,dn,sg,pt,kt,em,np,ar,rp,dl,fs,bp,wp,pc,mp,lr,cx,cr,pi,so,Rc,fa,ft,fe,ap,st,lc,Bl,sr,Qs,do,ld,dz,tc,ib,pl,sd,ll,rl,dl,Lt,ol,fl,lm,ts,rd,Dp,If! limits.c
LPATH=/usr/lib/hpux32:/opt/langtools/lib/hpux32
 /usr/ccs/bin/ld -o limits -u___exit -umain limits.o -lc
 removing /var/tmp/AAA019499
 removing limits.o
osipovmi@deblndw024v:~
$ ./limits
_XOPEN_PATH_MAX: 1024
PATH_MAX: 1023
_XOPEN_NAME_MAX: 255
NAME_MAX: 14
```
where `-D_HPUX_SOURCE` triggers `#define _INCLUDE_XOPEN_SOURCE_600` which in turn results in
```
 59 #ifdef _INCLUDE_XOPEN_SOURCE_600
 60 #  define _XOPEN_PATH_MAX  1024      /* Maximum number of bytes in a pathname */
 61 #  define _XOPEN_NAME_MAX  255       /* Maximum number of bytes in a filename */
 62 #endif /* _INCLUDE_XOPEN_SOURCE_600 */
```

How does this affect `openssl-rehash(1)`?

Have a look at this block: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/58d926213f00ba7046d0868de8b37929aa067a1f/apps/rehash.c#L45-L50 and this line: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/58d926213f00ba7046d0868de8b37929aa067a1f/apps/rehash.c#L374

Now run `openssl rehash /opt/openssl/certs` where you can find, e.g., `nss-129.crt` and ` siemens-pki-01.crt` along with others. While for the NSS cert the symlink is created, for the Siemens one it is not. Ran `tusc` on it and I see the following:
```
3156 lstat("/opt/openssl/certs/nss-129.crt", 0x7fffee50) .... = 0
3412 lstat("/opt/openssl/certs/siemens-extern", 0x7fffee50) . ERR#2 ENOENT
3413 lstat("/opt/openssl/certs/siemens-pki-01", 0x7fffee50) . ERR#2 ENOENT
```
The filename is successfully truncated down to 14 bytes making our certs not subject to hashing. Annoying is that this goes completely silent/unnoticed.

`rehash.c` has to be changed in a way that if first tries `_XOPEN_*_MAX` macros and then the regular `*_MAX` macros.

Note: files *are* available:

review_comments:
I see from the comment where this minimal size is derived from, but immediately below line 425 there is this code:
```
BIO_snprintf(buf, buflen, "%s%s%08x.%s%d",
                                 dirname, pathsep, bp->hash,
                                 suffixes[bp->type], nextid);
```

If the target dirname is short (say its just ./) and the file names are likewise short, it seems that fname_max_length will never get increased, but be insufficient for a maximially sized hash/type/id tuple

The dirname and pathsep is accounted for separately. The maximum length of %08x.%s%d is 20 (type is at most one character). In reality it will be much shorter as the nextid value will be a small number.
